faq: What is the Agentic AI Foundation?
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) is a neutral, open foundation hosted at the Linux Foundation that supports the open protocols and tools for AI agents, formed in December 2025.
Is AAIF controlled by one AI company?

No. The Agentic AI Foundation is a neutral foundation hosted at the Linux Foundation, with founding contributions from Member Org Two, Member Org Three and Member Org Eight and Platinum members including Member Org One, Member Org Six and Member Org Seven.
Which projects did the foundation launch with?
It launched with three founding contributions: Member Org Two's Model Context Protocol (MCP), Member Org Three's goose and Member Org Eight's AGENTS.md.

AAIF hosts:
- Agent Router
- Agent Skills
- Agent2Agent (A2A)
- AGENTS.md
- agentgateway
- Goose
- Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Open Responses
- OpenEnv
- OpenSandbox
How do I propose a new project to AAIF?
How much does membership cost, and what does each tier include?

Platinum membership is $350,000 a year and Gold $200,000; Silver is priced by company size from $5,000 to $75,000, and Associate membership is open to pre-approved non-profits and universities at no cost.
The press release names Member Org One, Member Org Two, Member Org Three, Member Org Four, Member Org Five, Member Org Six, Member Org Seven and Member Org Eight as Platinum members.
Join a working group, contribute to a hosted project on GitHub, or become an AAIF ambassador; the Get Involved menu on the site lists each path.
Where can I follow the foundation's news?
The site publishes a blog, press and news, a weekly briefing and a daily agentic AI newsletter, each with a subscription link.
